title: The Koszul projective resolution with its quotient augmentation
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $I$ an ideal, $r$ a natural number, and $f:\operatorname{Fin}(r)\to A$ a Koszul-regular sequence [def-weil-pbc-koszul-regular-sequence] with $(f)=I$. There exist a projective resolution $P$ of the $A$-module $A/I$ and a chain isomorphism $a:K_A(f)\cong P_\bullet$ [def-weil-pbc-koszul-complex] such that $a_0$ followed by the degree-zero augmentation of $P$ is the quotient map $\bigwedge_A^0 A^r\cong A\to A/I$. Empty sequences and unit ideals are included.

source.place: duality.tex, lemma-regular-immersion-ext, finite free Koszul resolution; Tags 0623 and 062E for the differential and regularity

proof.text: Import the existing private degree-one formula koszulBoundary_zero_quotient_formula from KoszulProjectiveResolution with a proof-only import all. Define the quotient augmentation using the degree-zero exterior equivalence. The imported formula identifies contraction in degree one with the generator linear combination, whose image is I, so the augmentation kills the differential.

Surjectivity of the quotient and equality of its kernel with the image of the first differential prove degree-zero quasi-isomorphism by the cokernel property. Koszul regularity gives exactness in all positive degrees; the target single complex is exact there.

The standard exterior basis makes each term projective. Bundle the exact original Koszul complex, the specified augmentation and these proofs as P; take a to be the identity isomorphism. Its degree-zero normalization is the constructed augmentation equality.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_koszul_normalized_projective_resolution
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] (I : Ideal A) (r : ℕ) (f : Fin r → A)
    (hreg : RingTheory.Sequence.IsKoszulRegular f) (hf : Ideal.span (Set.range f) = I) :
    ∃ P : ProjectiveResolution (ModuleCat.of A (A ⧸ I)),
      ∃ a : koszulComplex A r f ≅ P.complex,
        a.hom.f 0 ≫ P.π.f 0 =
          ModuleCat.ofHom (I.mkQ.comp
            (exteriorPower.zeroEquiv A (Fin r →₀ A)).toLinearMap)
